summary: I took the conventions from primary sources: recent bank 'Discussion Materials' that Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Evercore, Rothschild & Co and Centerview filed on SEC EDGAR as EX-99.(c) exhibits (2023-2026). I looked at the page images and sampled their colours. Pitchbook pages are US Letter landscape (11x8.5in, ratio 1.294) and Rothschild uses 4:3; none of the samples is 16:9. The report-kit page container should therefore default to 1056x816 CSS px, with A4 and 16:9 as options. Every page has the same parts: a section tracker, a one-sentence action title, a units line ('($ in millions, except per share data)'), navy chart banners, the chart or table with a commentary or key-figures side panel, numbered footnotes, a mandatory 'Source:' line with the as-of date, a draft or confidential stamp, and a page number. Colour use is restrained: a navy primary, steel-blue for the comparison series, greys, one accent, and a red or claret dashed line for the offer price. The subject company versus its peers is shown by emphasis, not by giving each company its own colour. I built 3 themes (navy, bronze, slate). Each has structural tokens plus an 8-colour categorical palette in light and dark versions, and all 6 palettes pass every hard check of the dataviz validator (contrast, colour-blind separation, lightness and chroma). Each theme also has a validated single-hue ramp, a sequential ramp and a diverging ramp. Number formatting differs by 'house style' (GS writes '$ 44.71' and '7.6 x'; others write '$2.27' and '7.9x'), so the format layer needs configurable presets. Fixed rules across houses: negatives in parentheses; n.m. kept out of mean/median; n.a. and the dash kept distinct; units only on the first and total rows; and think-cell-style rounding so displayed parts add up to the displayed total. The wish-list has 34 components with data fields and encodings. The 12 must-have components are: football field, share price + volume + events, indexed performance, comps table, precedents table, sensitivity grid, waterfall, analysis at various prices, premiums paid, multiple history with '% of time in range', financial summary, and think-cell-style columns (CAGR arrows, difference arrows, value lines, totals). Engine: keep ECharts 6.1 (already vendored, Apache-2.0). Version 6 adds axis breaks, a matrix layout, chord diagrams, beeswarm/jitter and runtime theme switching including dark mode. Add the official @echarts-x/custom-bar-range (1.8KB auto-registering classic script) for range bars and simple-statistics for regression and quantiles. Use HTML tables for comps, sensitivity and AVP so they can be copied into Excel, and Tabulator only if heavy grid interaction is needed. License and offline hazards: ApexCharts 8 is now free only below $2M revenue, MapLibre GL 6 ships only ES modules (fails under file://), lightweight-charts requires TradingView attribution, GSAP's license is not OSI-approved, and Plotly is 1.44MB gzipped and pulls map data from a CDN by default.

libraries.name: Apache ECharts
libraries.capabilities: Main engine for most of the IB canon: line, bar, stacked and 100% stacked bars, waterfall (via stacked or custom series), candlestick, scatter/bubble, heatmap, treemap, sankey, chord, boxplot, map. Version 6 adds axis breaks, a matrix layout (small multiples and table-like layouts), beeswarm/jitter, runtime theme switching and dark mode, and endLabel, markLine, markArea and markPoint for event annotation.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x/y position, symbolSize (bubble area), color via visualMap (continuous or piecewise), symbol shape, opacity, label; geo color plus scatter size for proportional symbols
libraries.interactions_animation: dataZoom (inside and slider), brush, legend toggling, tooltip crosshair, echarts.connect for linked panes, universalTransition morphing on data change, animation easing and stagger
libraries.reason: Already vendored, permissive license, broadest IB coverage, classic-script build works under file://, and the SVG renderer prints sharply.

libraries.name: @echarts-x/custom-bar-range (official echarts-custom-series)
libraries.capabilities: Reusable barRange custom series (low-high bars) for ECharts 6. Fits football fields, 52-week ranges, SOTP ranges and Gantt-like bars. The sibling packages line-range, violin, contour and segmented doughnut can give a +/-1 sigma band for multiple history.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/bar-range.auto.min.js (1.8KB) auto-registers on the global echarts.
libraries.reason: Tiny official extension that renders the football field directly, so no hand-rolled custom renderItem is needed.

libraries.name: D3
libraries.capabilities: Low-level toolkit for bespoke IB visuals ECharts does poorly: Marimekko with variable widths, market-map tile layouts, custom callout and annotation layers, d3-scale/d3-shape helpers.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: any (full control of position, size, color, shape)
libraries.reason: Use selectively for Marimekko, market maps and annotation layers. It costs more code per chart than ECharts.

libraries.name: d3-svg-annotation (d3-annotation)
libraries.capabilities: Callout annotations (labels with connectors, badges, threshold lines) for event markers on price charts.
libraries.reason: Unmaintained since 2019. Borrow the callout design (GS-style boxed callouts, MS letter badges) and implement it with ECharts graphic/markPoint.

libraries.name: Observable Plot
libraries.capabilities: Concise grammar for dot strips, small multiples (facets), regression (linearRegressionY), box plots, waffles and ranges; good for prototyping distribution and ranking charts.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/plot.umd.min.js, but it needs the global d3 UMD loaded first.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, fill, stroke, r (size), symbol, opacity, facets
libraries.reason: Good secondary option for statistical and faceted views. Limited animation and no IB decorations, so it should not be the main engine.

libraries.name: Vega + Vega-Lite + vega-embed
libraries.capabilities: Declarative JSON grammar (layer, facet, concat, regression/loess transforms, selections, cross-filtering). An ideal output format for a step-2 local LLM that generates chart specs from a client's question.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: build/vega.min.js and build/vega-lite.min.js UMD (globals vega, vegaLite). Data must be inline values; url loaders fail under file://.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, row/column facets
libraries.interactions_animation: param-based selections, brush, cross-filter; minimal animation
libraries.reason: Defer to step 2: a JSON spec is a safe sandbox for LLM-generated charts. Its look needs heavy theming to match pitchbooks.

libraries.name: Chart.js
libraries.capabilities: Canvas charts with native floating bars ([low, high] data), which gives quick football fields and waterfalls. Plugins add annotation, zoom, matrix (heatmap), sankey and treemap.
libraries.reason: Solid and permissive, but it duplicates ECharts, which is already vendored and stronger for linked panes, maps and decorations.

libraries.name: chartjs-plugin-annotation
libraries.capabilities: Lines, boxes, labels and points for Chart.js: offer-price lines and event callouts.
libraries.reason: Only relevant if Chart.js is adopted, which is not recommended.

libraries.name: chartjs-chart-matrix
libraries.capabilities: Matrix/heatmap cells for Chart.js; could render sensitivity grids.
libraries.reason: Sensitivity, accretion/dilution and AVP grids should be HTML tables (copyable, accessible, sharp in print), not canvas.

libraries.name: Plotly.js (plotly.js-dist-min)
libraries.capabilities: Native waterfall, funnel, treemap, sunburst, sankey, choropleth, 3D, financial OHLC.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: plotly.min.js, but geo charts fetch topojson from a CDN by default (topojsonURL must be overridden).
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, size, color, symbol, facets
libraries.reason: Too heavy for self-contained client folders, and its default look is scientific rather than pitchbook. Its strengths are already covered by ECharts.

libraries.name: uPlot
libraries.capabilities: Very fast time-series lines and areas (millions of points), with cursor sync across charts.
libraries.reason: Fallback for very dense daily price histories of many tickers if ECharts sampling is not enough. Plain styling.

libraries.name: TradingView lightweight-charts
libraries.license: Apache-2.0 plus a TradingView attribution requirement (NOTICE text and a visible link to tradingview.com)
libraries.capabilities: Candlestick, OHLC, line, area, histogram (volume), price lines, markers; trading-terminal UX.
libraries.reason: The attribution clause puts third-party branding in client deliverables, and the trading-terminal look is not pitchbook style. ECharts covers price + volume + events.

libraries.name: ApexCharts
libraries.license: Dual license (8.x LICENSE.md): the Community License is free only for organisations under $2M annual revenue; banks need a paid Commercial/OEM license
libraries.capabilities: Wide range of SVG chart types with good default animation.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (UMD), but the license blocks it
libraries.reason: The 2026 license change makes it commercial for any investment bank. Not permissive.

libraries.name: Highcharts
libraries.capabilities: Highcharts Stock (navigator, flags for events), variwide/Marimekko, waterfall, annotations, accessibility module.
libraries.reason: Commercial license. Useful as a design reference for stock flags/annotations and variwide charts.

libraries.name: amCharts 5
libraries.license: Commercial (the free version requires an amCharts branding link)
libraries.capabilities: Stock charts, maps, flow diagrams, rich animation.
libraries.reason: Commercial or branded. Reference for animation feel only.

libraries.name: billboard.js
libraries.capabilities: D3-based C3 successor: line/bar/area/gauge/radar; table-view and text-overlap plugins.
libraries.reason: Overlaps with ECharts while offering fewer IB chart types and decorations, at a large size.

libraries.name: Tabulator
libraries.capabilities: Interactive data grid: sorting, filtering, grouping (peer sub-groups), frozen columns, column calcs (mean/median rows), formatters, CSV/XLSX export, clipboard.
libraries.interactions_animation: sort/filter/group, row selection events usable for cross-filtering
libraries.reason: Good if comps or precedents need heavy interaction. Plain HTML tables plus a small sort/filter layer may be enough for most pages.

libraries.name: AG Grid Community
libraries.capabilities: High-performance grid, filtering, sorting, cell renderers. Pivoting, row grouping aggregation and integrated charts are Enterprise-only.
libraries.reason: Only if very large tables are required. Watch the Enterprise boundary and the size.

libraries.name: Grid.js
libraries.capabilities: Lightweight table with search, sort and pagination.
libraries.reason: Stagnant since 2024 and lacks grouping and column calcs.

libraries.name: frappe-gantt
libraries.capabilities: Interactive SVG Gantt (tasks, dependencies, day/week/month views) for deal timelines.
libraries.reason: Usable for interactive timelines. Printed pitchbook timelines are better as a CSS grid with milestone diamonds.

libraries.name: vis-timeline
libraries.capabilities: Zoomable timeline/scheduler with groups and items.
libraries.reason: Heavy, scheduler-style look that does not fit pitchbook aesthetics.

libraries.name: simple-statistics
libraries.capabilities: linearRegression, rSquared, quantile/percentile, median, mean, standardDeviation. Feeds comps stats rows (Max/75th/Median/Mean/25th/Min), regression scatter and premiums percentiles.
libraries.reason: Tiny, permissive, and exactly the statistics IB tables need, so they don't have to be re-implemented.

libraries.name: d3-format
libraries.capabilities: Spec-based number formatting (SI prefixes, currency, locale).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (inside d3.min.js or its own UMD)
libraries.reason: The kit already has Excel-style rk.format, which analysts know better. Borrow locale ideas only.

libraries.name: numbro / numeral
libraries.capabilities: Number formatting with abbreviations and locales.
libraries.reason: Stagnant. Intl.NumberFormat plus rk.format with house-style presets cover these needs.

libraries.name: Leaflet
libraries.capabilities: Choropleth and proportional-symbol footprint maps (revenue by region, asset locations), clusters, heat layers.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/leaflet.js (already in vendor/leaflet with markercluster and heat)
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: fill color (choropleth), circle radius (sqrt-scaled size), marker shape, opacity
libraries.reason: Already vendored, permissive, and works with the offline world-atlas TopoJSON.

libraries.name: MapLibre GL JS
libraries.capabilities: WebGL vector-tile maps, 3D extrusion, data-driven styling.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No for 6.x: it ships only dist/maplibre-gl.mjs (ES modules). Version 5.24.0 still ships dist/maplibre-gl.js UMD.
libraries.reason: The ESM-only 6.x breaks under file://. If vector maps are ever needed, pin 5.24.0; otherwise Leaflet is enough for pitchbook maps.

libraries.name: GSAP
libraries.capabilities: High-end timeline animation, ScrollTrigger, SVG morphing.
libraries.reason: Non-OSI license with usage restrictions. Pitchbook motion (line reveal, bar growth, count-up, morph on update) is achievable with ECharts animation, CSS and the Web Animations API.

libraries.name: FT chart-doctor / Visual Vocabulary
libraries.license: MIT (code); poster content is copyright The Financial Times
libraries.capabilities: Taxonomy of 9 chart families (deviation, correlation, ranking, distribution, change over time, magnitude, part-to-whole, spatial, flow) with about 70 chart forms; Chinese posters exist.
libraries.reason: Use as the gallery/navigation taxonomy and map IB charts onto it. Do not copy the poster artwork.

libraries.name: @financial-times/o-colors
libraries.capabilities: Shows the FT palette structure (paper, claret, oxford, teal, slate with tones).
libraries.reason: Brand palette, so take inspiration from its structure (paper background, one claret accent) without copying the hex values.

libraries.name: think-cell
libraries.capabilities: What bankers build in PowerPoint: stacked/clustered/100% bars, waterfall, Mekko (unit and % axes), Gantt, scatter/bubble, combination; decorations (CAGR arrows, difference arrows, value lines, totals, axis breaks, Other grouping, Harvey balls); TCROUND sum-consistent rounding; Excel/JSON data links.
libraries.reason: The target look and decoration vocabulary for the kit's column, waterfall and Mekko components and its rounding utility.

libraries.name: Arimo / Tinos (Fontsource)
libraries.capabilities: Metric-compatible with Arial and Times New Roman, so line breaks match client PowerPoint/Excel. Latin woff2 is about 11.4KB per weight.
libraries.offline_classic_script: woff2 + CSS @font-face; place under ./fonts next to index.html or base64-inline (Firefox file:// rule).
libraries.reason: Gives the banker sans look under a permissive license with tiny files.

libraries.name: Source Serif 4 / Inter / IBM Plex (Fontsource)
libraries.capabilities: Serif action titles for the boutique/bronze theme; Inter (tabular numerals) and IBM Plex Sans/Mono for the modern slate theme and formula input.
libraries.reason: High-quality open faces that cover all 3 themes.

libraries.name: Noto Sans SC / TC (Fontsource, Source Han Sans family)
libraries.capabilities: Chinese UI and report text. One weight is about 3.4MB split into 102 unicode-range woff2 chunks.
libraries.offline_classic_script: woff2 + CSS; must be subset (pyftsubset in the Python builder) and inlined for file://
libraries.reason: Needed for Chinese clients and labels, but only after per-report subsetting.

key_insights: Page size: US bank pitchbooks are US Letter landscape (11x8.5in, aspect 1.294), verified on GS, Morgan Stanley and Evercore EDGAR page images. Rothschild uses 4:3 and none of the samples is 16:9. Default the page container to 1056x816 CSS px with @page size 11in 8.5in, and offer A4 landscape (EMEA/Asia) and 16:9.

Page anatomy is consistent across all banks: section tracker (caps label, navy tab, or footer section name), action title, units line '($ in millions, except per share data)', navy banner chart headers, a side panel (commentary bullets with bold lead-ins, or a 'Select data points' KPI table), superscript-numbered footnotes, a mandatory 'Source:' line with the as-of date, a draft/confidential stamp, and a page number. Footnote numbering should be automated per page.

Colour is semantic emphasis, not categorical. Subject company = dark navy, peers = steel-blue or grey, mean/median = dashed lines, offer/current price = red or claret dashed reference line with an italic label, 'For reference only' methods = light/grey bars. Typically 4-5 colours per page.

Validated palettes (all PASS in both light and dark mode). navy light: #2e64a6,#b68028,#9f3960,#4b99c9,#57873a,#7555a8,#cb5f31,#008e88; navy dark (#0f1724): #4c82c6,#bd8630,#b74e74,#449fc9,#639346,#8a69be,#d5683b,#129d97. bronze light (#fbf9f5): #aa6926,#37649e,#8f2c47,#a68922,#008b9d,#cb6443,#865695,#469364. slate light: #3e6dc8,#db6143,#009783,#7d5abc,#3e9245,#379fc7,#c38700,#c35f92. The first 3 colours of each also pass all-pairs checks for scatter, bubble and map charts.

Navy structural tokens: ink #0b2545 (15.4:1), banner #12355f (white text 12.4:1), navy-700 #1f4e79, steel #6f97c7, tint #e6edf6, stat-row #f2f4f7, muted #6b7280, gold accent #b68028, reference red #b3261e. Single-hue navy ramp #0e2a47,#1f4e79,#3a6fa6,#6b93c4,#98b4d8 passes the ordinal checks; use it for stacked segments to get the classic monochrome IB look.

Number formatting varies by house style (GS: '$ 44.71', '7.6 x', '(0.9)%', '05-Dec-2025'; others: '$2.27', '7.9x', '(32%)', 'Apr '24'; units mm/MM/m, bn/Bn). Make these configurable house-style settings in rk.format (currencySpace, multSpace, percent parentheses inside or outside, unit suffix, date styles) rather than hard-coding them.

Table rule from the GS DCF/AVP/precedents pages: only the first row and subtotal/total rows carry $, x or %; middle rows are bare numbers. Subtotals bold with a top rule, a dashed vertical line between stub/historical and projected columns, the terminal column shaded, the subject company row highlighted, and stats rows (Max/75th/Mean/Median/25th/Min) on a grey background separated from the data rows.

n.m. (not meaningful: negative denominator or multiple above a house threshold), n.a. (missing) and the dash (zero or not applicable) must stay distinct. n.m. values are excluded from mean/median, and the threshold goes in a footnote.

The core of think-cell is its decoration layer and rounding, not its chart types: CAGR arrows, difference arrows, value lines, totals, axis breaks, 'Other' grouping, automatic black/white label contrast, and TCROUND-style sum-consistent rounding. Build these as reusable decoration plugins plus a roundToTotal (largest-remainder) utility.

Event annotation on price charts comes in 3 bank styles, and the kit should support all 3: boxed callouts with leader lines colour-coded by event category (GS), lettered badges on the line plus an event table (MS), and vertical drop lines with a bold date and text (Rothschild). Also: an end-of-line last-value label, a 52-week high/low and VWAP mini-table, and an undisturbed-date marker.

IB convention often uses a dual y-axis (price + volume, or price + EV/NTM EBITDA), which data-viz best practice forbids. Default to vertically stacked panes sharing the x-axis (ECharts multi-grid plus a linked dataZoom), and keep a dualAxis option for house-style compatibility with both axes titled and unitised.

Sensitivity, accretion/dilution, analysis-at-various-prices, comps and precedents should be HTML tables (copyable as TSV to Excel, accessible, sharp in print) with a highlighted base-case cell and low-saturation sequential or diverging backgrounds. Recompute live from formulas (rk.expr) when the client changes the axis centre or step, or types a new metric column.

Football field implementation: a method column (navy tabs with white text, grouped primary vs reference), range bars with outside-end value labels, dashed reference lines (offer, unaffected VWAP, current), and optional right-hand columns for implied TEV, multiple and premium (Evercore style). @echarts-x/custom-bar-range (Apache-2.0, 1.8KB auto-registering classic script) renders the bars; the text columns are HTML grid.

ECharts 6 capabilities confirmed by grepping the vendored build: axis breaks, matrix coordinate system, chord, beeswarm/jitter, setTheme for runtime and dark-mode switching, universalTransition, relativeTo label anchoring. There is no native waterfall series, so use a stacked bar with a transparent base or a custom series. Use the SVG renderer for print/PDF.

2026 license and offline traps: ApexCharts 8.x is dual-licensed and free only below $2M revenue (avoid). MapLibre GL 6.x is ESM-only .mjs and breaks under file:// (the last UMD build is 5.24.0). lightweight-charts requires NOTICE text and a tradingview.com link. GSAP 3.15 uses a non-OSI 'Standard no charge' license. Plotly is 1.44MB gzipped and fetches topojson from a CDN by default. Observable Plot's UMD build needs global d3, and Vega-Lite's needs global vega.

Fonts: bulge brackets use all-sans Arial-like type (bold navy or black titles); boutiques use a large serif title with sans body. Open replacements: Arimo/Tinos (Arial/Times metric-compatible, OFL, about 11.4KB per latin weight), Source Serif 4, Inter, IBM Plex. Noto Sans SC is about 3.4MB per weight, so it must be subset by the Python builder. Under file://, Firefox only loads fonts from the same directory or a subdirectory, so put them in ./fonts/ or base64-inline them.

Map the FT Visual Vocabulary families (deviation, correlation, ranking, distribution, change over time, magnitude, part-to-whole, spatial, flow) to IB components for gallery navigation. IB-specific forms with no FT equivalent: football field (range/dumbbell), sensitivity grid (XY heatmap as a table), AVP table, league table, tombstones, Harvey-ball matrix.

Anthropic's financial-services repo (Apache-2.0) codifies Excel-model conventions usable as defaults: section header fill #1F4E79, column header #D9E1F2, stats rows #F2F2F2, key output/base case #BDD7EE bold, blue input / black formula / green link font colours, 1-decimal multiples and percents, parentheses for negatives, and 'only blues and greys, 3-4 colours total'.

Strong interaction patterns for client use: time-range presets (1M/3M/6M/1Y/3Y/5Y/Since unaffected) with linked zoom across price, indexed and multiple charts; brushing the regression scatter filters the comps table; an offer-price slider updates the football field reference line and AVP premiums live; a peer-sample filter recomputes the premiums-paid percentiles; a re-base-to-100 date picker on the indexed chart.

Motion for a pitchbook feel: line clip reveal over 600-900ms with cubicOut, bars growing from the baseline over 400-600ms with a 30ms stagger, universalTransition morphing on data updates, KPI count-up; disabled for prefers-reduced-motion and print.
